title: Yitzchak Resh Galuta
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: In [Yevamot 115b](https://www.sefaria.org/Yevamot.115b.8) (cited by Hyman as קמו:), he was Rav Bibi’s sister’s son. He was traveling from Kurtaba to Aspamya and died. Word was sent from there of his death. The Gemara asks whether there might be a second Yitzchak Resh Galuta. Hyman reports that [Seder HaDorot](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=2180&lang=en) cites [the Rosh’s responsa](https://www.sefaria.org/Teshuvot_HaRosh.51.2), klal 50, for the view that this was his name and that he did not hold the office of Exilarch. The argument is that one would hardly raise a doubt about a second Yitzchak Resh Galuta if this were the Exilarch known throughout the Diaspora.[^1][^2][^3]

notes.text: Hyman’s printed locator is 146b. The linked Yevamot 115b names Yitzchak as the son of Rav Bibi’s sister, then raises the possibility of a second man with the same name.
Heilprin cites Yevamot 115b and brings the byname argument in the name of the Rosh’s responsa.
In the linked Teshuvot HaRosh 51:2, the opening letter assumes he held the office. The reply to “my father” argues that Resh Galuta was a byname or family name. Hyman and Heilprin cite klal 50.
